prompts: Words are tied to each other, and nobody here can see how. {WS}/site is a saved copy of a Portuguese creative dictionary. Explore this universe of words: collect what the site knows and build {WS}/universe/index.html, a single file that sums the universe up in one view and lets someone search for a word and find how it relates to others. The best way to show it is your call, and that view is what we care about most. So people can share a word, opening the page with ?word=saudade must show that word and its relations. Save the data as {WS}/words.json, mapping each word to the words it is linked to, and record in {WS}/result.json: words (how many), relations (how many distinct pairs) and most_connected. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
The site is 256 static HTML pages, one per word, with "Sinônimos" and "Palavras análogas" sections. I'll parse them with a Node script, then build a self-contained interactive page.Three dangling targets are redirect pages (meta refresh). I'll follow redirects and skip the homepage draft link.Data verified. Now the visualization page — 2D canvas force graph, embedded data, search + shareable `?word=` URLs.Now verify it live in the browser at `file://` with `?word=saudade`:The share view works. Quick test of search and clicking a related word:Verified `?word=MAR` resolves via case-insensitive fallback. Cross-checking one page against the source for proof:[goal] Sum up the Portuguese creative dictionary in ./site into one shareable, searchable view.

[action] Parsed all 256 HTML pages, extracted words, themes and the "Sinônimos" / "Palavras análogas" links, built the data files and a self-contained visualization, then verified it live in a browser.

[result]
- `./words.json` — 250 words, each mapped to its linked words.
- `./result.json` — words: 250, relations: 743 distinct pairs, most_connected: tempo 16, palavra 16, pescador/advogado/capital/alma/almoço/madrugada/pais/herança 9 each.
- `./universe/index.html` — a single ~37 KB file, no build step. It embeds the data inline (so it works from `file://`, where `fetch` of a sibling JSON is blocked) and only touches Google Fonts externally (the three.js CDN was allowed but a dependency-free canvas force graph is more reliable). It shows: a force-directed graph of all 250 words colored by theme (10 themes), drag/zoom, hover tooltips, a search box with suggestions, a side panel listing a word's relations (clickable to hop through the network), and a copy-link button.

Assumptions I made, where the brief left room:
- A "word page" is any page with an `<h1>` plus a `Tema:` paragraph; 6 of the 256 files are index/about/contact/redirects, so 250 word pages = 250 words.
- Relations come only from the "Sinônimos" and "Palavras análogas" sections; header/footer "palavras do dia" and "mais buscadas" links are navigation, not semantics, and are excluded.
- Three redirect stubs (saudades→saudade, corações→coração, paixões→paixão) are followed; 5 links to pages that don't exist (em-construcao, pagina-removida, etc.) are dropped; one link to the homepage draft (rascunho-3.html) is dropped.
- Links are treated as undirected: if A lists B, the edge counts even if B doesn't list A back (e.g. Mar.html lists flor/vale, which therefore appear in mar's relations).

How I know it is right:
- `?word=saudade` opened over `file://` shows saudade centered, highlighted, with its 5 relations (ansiedade, carinho, dor, esperança, nostalgia) matching site/saudade.html's sections exactly (screenshot above).
- `?word=MAR` (uppercase) falls back case-insensitively to "mar" and shows its 7 relations; site/Mar.html's own lists account for lago, onda, flor, vale, medo, with floresta and pétala coming from the reciprocal links on those pages.
- Search tested live: typing "caf" suggests "café" (comida); selecting it updates the URL to `?word=caf%C3%A9` and lists água, chá, momento, pimenta, trabalho.
- The pair count 743 was computed from a set of undirected pairs; per-word sums are consistent with it.

[next] Ready for review as-is; if the reviewer wants relations split by type (synonym vs analog) or a 3D three.js render, that data could be added without changing the file structure.
